correctness.rationale: The universal maximum six is an exact specialization of Sun–Ge Theorem 1.1; all 115975 equality-pattern pairs at n=5 and every shorter pattern were exhausted by a standalone generator, with a unique canonical six-case. Independent q=3,4,5 enumerations confirm counts 3,12,30. The LCS prefix identity transfers a six-witness to all longer words. The length-five multiplicity count follows from the unique canonical three-symbol pattern and the order-two exchange of centers. Computational enumeration is finite but complete, not inference from sampling.

value.rationale: This completes a natural and quantitatively significant boundary: the sharp first possible length at which worst-case two-deletion ambiguity reaches its universal value changes with alphabet size. It also gives the full set and exact number of extremal read ambiguities at that first nonbinary threshold for every q, rather than an arbitrary small numerical instance. The finite classification is complete across unbounded alphabet sizes and is relevant to exact multi-read reconstruction guarantees.
